clue.text: Veto the elevation of dull little man

parts.note: to veto something is to ban it

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevating a word means reading it upwards, so backwards

parts.note: mat (or matt) describes a dull, unshiny finish

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to let a boring little fellow get a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the elevation of' turns MAT upwards to TAM in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A bantam is a small breed of fowl, and by extension a small but feisty person.

clue.text: Revealing a gap caused by boring?

definitions.meaning: a chasm that gapes wide open
the involuntary open-mouthed reflex brought on by tedium, with boring read as tedious rather than drilling

explanation.surface: A hole appears where someone has been drilling.
explanation.definitionFit: A yawning chasm is wide open, and a dull lecture makes the audience open their mouths wearily.

clue.text: Settle on woven cane maybe

parts.note: a bird settles on a branch, it perches

indicators.note: weaving twists strands together, so the letters of cane are interlaced into a new order

explanation.surface: A bird lands on some wicker basketwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woven' rearranges CANE into ANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Perchance is an old-fashioned word for perhaps.

clue.text: The main holiday

parts.note: the main is the open sea, so a holiday on it is a trip aboard a liner

explanation.surface: The chief vacation of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'main' looks like 'principal' but is the old poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A voyage taken for pleasure on an ocean liner is a seaborne vacation.

clue.text: A French lie giving rise to some agitation

parts.note: un is the French for a
to lie down is to rest

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's falsehood stirs up trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrest is disturbance or turmoil among people.

clue.text: Drawn out in awkward fashion

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters of drawn out are remade in a new order

explanation.surface: Something is stretched out clumsily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' is a verb here: the letters of DRAWN OUT are fashioned into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means inconvenient or unfortunate, the kind of thing that makes a situation uncomfortable.

clue.text: Woman stuffing a carrier in Burlington house

indicators.note: one thing stuffing another is packed inside it

parts.note: Burlington House in London is the home of the RA, the Royal Academy of Arts
a hod is a builder's trough for carrying bricks

explanation.surface: A lady fills a bag at a grand London mansion.
explanation.walkthrough: Burlington House, on Piccadilly in London, houses the Royal Academy, abbreviated RA; HOD goes between R and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhoda is a female first name.

clue.text: One who looks for cunning in a forecaster

indicators.note: the word for cunning sits in the middle of the word for forecaster

parts.note: a seer foretells the future
arch means sly or knowingly cunning

explanation.surface: A clever weatherman goes looking for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hunts or seeks things is a seeker, one engaged in a search.

clue.text: As mature as laymen can be

indicators.note: suggests the letters of as mature could be turned into something else

explanation.surface: Ordinary people may be as grown-up as anyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' rearranges AS MATURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Laymen are non-professionals, people who are not experts in a field.

clue.text: Making to turn to a fellow Turk

indicators.note: making the first to turn means writing that word backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
taken as written
a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: Someone sets out to approach a Turkish man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' makes the first TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ottomans were the Turkish dynasty and people of the Ottoman Empire.

clue.text: Having nervous trouble hold on — get a pick-me-up

indicators.note: the word for nervous trouble holds the other word inside it

parts.note: a tic is a nervous twitch
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone with jittery nerves is told to hang on and take a restorative.
explanation.definitionFit: A tonic is a restorative drink or medicine that perks you up.

clue.text: Measured progress of owls seen about early in the year

indicators.note: about here means turned around, so the letters of owls are rearranged

parts.note: March is the third month, early in the calendar

explanation.surface: Owls are spotted in spring, making steady headway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges OWLS into SLOW; 'seen' just links.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow march is a deliberate, stately military pace used at ceremonies.

clue.text: Means to buy — but not now

definitions.text: Means to buy — but not now

parts.words: Means to buy — but not now
parts.note: money once used to pay for goods in Britain but no longer current

explanation.surface: Funds for shopping that are no longer valid.
explanation.walkthrough: Before decimalisation in 1971, British money was counted in pounds, shillings and pence, written £sd from the Latin librae, solidi, denarii.
explanation.definitionFit: Pounds, shillings and pence was the old British currency system, abolished in 1971.

clue.text: Ships' officers going around and giving orders

indicators.note: the officers surround the linking word

parts.note: mates are officers on merchant ships
taken as written

explanation.surface: Naval officers walk around issuing commands.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandates are official commands or authorisations.

clue.text: Angered about article, so complained

indicators.note: the word for angered goes around the article

parts.note: riled means made angry
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone, irked by a newspaper piece, grumbled.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to protest bitterly, to grumble loudly against something.

clue.text: Lawyers who might get a cad's vote

indicators.note: suggests the letters of a cad's vote could be turned into something

parts.note: the s of the possessive counts as a letter here

explanation.surface: Barristers who might win the ballot of a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might get' rearranges A CADS VOTE, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Advocates are barristers, especially in Scotland, who plead cases in court.

clue.text: Such jocularity can be distressing for the elderly

parts.note: a bad experience is a distressing one
being in age means being old, the condition of the elderly

explanation.surface: Teasing banter can upset old people.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as BAD IN AGE: something bad in old age distresses the elderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is witty, playful teasing conversation.

clue.text: The car component appeared incomplete

indicators.note: the word for appeared is left without its final letter

parts.note: came means arrived or appeared

explanation.surface: A part of the car turned up unfinished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'incomplete' cuts the last letter from CAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A cam is a rotating engine part that opens and closes the valves.

clue.text: Stayed in custody

definitions.meaning: halted or checked, as when progress is stopped

explanation.surface: Someone remained locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay something is to halt it, as is to arrest development; and a suspect held by police has been detained.

clue.text: A cleric finding what a computer can do

parts.note: DD stands for Doctor of Divinity, a churchman's degree

explanation.surface: A clergyman discovers the abilities of a computer.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding up sums is a basic arithmetic operation a machine performs.

clue.text: Less hirsute son of Odin

definitions.meaning: having less hair on the head
the Norse god of light and beauty, killed by mistletoe

explanation.surface: A Norse god's son with thinning hair.
explanation.walkthrough: In Norse myth, Balder (or Baldur) is the son of Odin and Frigg.
explanation.definitionFit: Hirsute means hairy, so its opposite is more hairless; the Norse god shares the same spelling.

clue.text: In quest of the mute swan or other large bird

indicators.note: the bird lies in the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Searching for the silent swan, or some other big bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' points inside 'the mute'; 'quest of' and 'swan or' dress the surface. The bird is other than a swan.
explanation.definitionFit: The emu is a large flightless Australian bird.

clue.text: Cut due — about to clean up

indicators.note: the word due wraps around the other piece
in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: to lave is to wash or clean

explanation.surface: A payment owed is reduced, ahead of a tidy-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reads the washing word bottom to top in this down clue, and 'about' wraps the owed word round it. 'Cut' looks like a noun after the dash but is a verb meaning reduce.
explanation.definitionFit: To devalue is to reduce the worth of something, cutting its value.

clue.text: The leading lady maybe says more

indicators.note: suggests the letters of says more are only one possible arrangement

explanation.surface: The star actress perhaps has extra lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges SAYS MORE. 'The leading lady' is not an actress but the first lady of a town.
explanation.definitionFit: A mayoress is a woman mayor or the mayor's wife, a town's chief civic lady.

clue.text: Serve a non-drinker, getting a tip

parts.note: TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: A waiter serves a teetotaller and receives a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' looks like a gratuity in this restaurant scene but is END.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend on someone is to wait on or serve them.

clue.text: The person posing as an easy target

definitions.meaning: a model sitting for a portrait painter
a chance so simple to take that missing it would be shameful

explanation.surface: The model is a sitting duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sits for an artist is a model; and in sport an easy catch or shot is called by the same word.

clue.text: Select, unmarried, and striking

parts.note: single means not married
workers on strike are said to be out

explanation.surface: A chosen bachelor who is also very good-looking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'striking' looks like 'handsome' but means on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To single out is to pick out one from a group for special attention.

clue.text: Fly powerless to obtain notes about cover

indicators.note: the two notes sit on either side of the word for cover

parts.note: G and E are musical notes
a lid covers a pot

explanation.surface: Flying without an engine needs musical notes and a cover.
explanation.definitionFit: Gliding is flying without an engine, riding the air currents.

clue.text: Pop back with some pictures alone

indicators.note: the word for pop is taken back to front

parts.note: pa and pop are both words for father
paintings and drawings collectively are art

explanation.surface: Dad returns with a few photos all by himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns PA into AP.
explanation.definitionFit: Being apart means being separate, away from others.

clue.text: Spread out and read it — a mistake

indicators.note: signals the letters of read it a have been set down wrongly and need reordering

explanation.surface: Someone tells a reader that the text is a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' rearranges READ IT A.
explanation.definitionFit: To radiate is to spread outward from a centre, like rays.

clue.text: Popular river's about dry. That could be dangerous

indicators.note: the river is set around, beside, the word for dry

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
sec is French for dry, used of wine
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A favourite river nearly runs dry, which could be hazardous.
explanation.walkthrough: SEC is the wine term for dry; the Ure is a Yorkshire river.
explanation.definitionFit: Something insecure is unsafe or unstable, liable to give way.

clue.text: Looked at the guy left in bed

indicators.note: the guy and left are placed inside the bed

parts.note: taken as written
he refers to a man

explanation.surface: A man was observed lying in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Beheld is the past tense of behold, to see or observe.
